correctness.rationale: For any simple closed triangular cellulation, each odd-valence vertex with no monochromatic incident edge must lie opposite one in a triangular face: otherwise its odd neighbor link would be properly 2-colored, impossible. Every monochromatic edge covers at most its two endpoints and the two opposite-face vertices, yielding o<=4b, hence ceil(o/4). On the explicit icosahedral graph, independent exhaustive base-three enumeration of every 3^12=531441 labeled assignment recomputed the exact 13 occupancy-sector minima (10,8,6,4,3,4,5,8,11,15,20,25,30) and minimizing degeneracies (72,600,1260,360,120,360,120,480,240,160,144,24,1), plus exactly 20 three-defect supports each supporting 6 colorings. The lower convex envelope has the seven stated vertices and slopes -2,-1,1,3,4,5; independent exact counting corroborated crossing multiplicities (2292,480,600,840,400,329). For this finite graph the exhaustive state space and graph construction are complete, not a sample or infinite extrapolation. Original C++ exhaustive and separate 9-state column transfer code inspected, and the parity bound checked mathematically.

originality.rationale: The complete q=3 icosahedral finite field-sector classification and odd-valence monochromatic-bond obstruction are distinct from neighboring published q=4 icosahedral Potts counts and from infinite-lattice 3-state results. Nakamoto–Ota–Watanabe primary full text treats maxima of vividly colored faces, not a lower bound on monochromatic edges for every arbitrary coloring. Earlier indexed Potts/coloring tables and folklore forms of the o/4 bound remain a meaningful historical risk; not a decisive mathematical coverage source in inspected material.
residual_risks: Finite icosahedral enumeration counts all labeled configurations exactly and does not establish any infinite cluster or finite temperature phase transition.
Potential unindexed icosahedral Potts tables and equivalent defective-coloring formulations remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The icosahedral graph is a canonical highly frustrated 12-site triangulated spherical cluster; its complete one-color-field Potts magnetic staircase, exact degeneracies and geometrically organized twenty defect supports are natural finite invariants not obtained by a known table. The general odd-degree obstruction offers structural motivation, and the exhaustive result answers a precisely delineated finite-cluster question; no thermodynamic phase transition is asserted.

limitations: Finite icosahedral enumeration counts all labeled configurations exactly and does not establish any infinite cluster or finite temperature phase transition.
Potential unindexed icosahedral Potts tables and equivalent defective-coloring formulations remain priority risks.
